en: Ishaq ibn Mansur narrated to us: Abu Asim informed us, from Yazid ibn Abi Ubayd, from Salamah ibn al-Akwa': that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Whoever among you offers a sacrifice, let there not remain anything of it in his house after three days." When the following year came, they said: "O Messenger of Allah, should we do as we did in the first year?" He said: "No, for that was a year in which the people were facing hardship, so I wanted it to be distributed among them."

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Abd al-A'la narrated to us, from al-Jurayri, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri (H); and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Abd al-A'la narrated to us: Sa'id narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Abu Nadrah, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "O people of Medina, do not eat the meat of sacrificial animals beyond three"—and Ibn al-Muthanna said: "three days." They complained to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) that they had dependents, retinues, and servants. So he said: "Eat, feed others, and withhold or store." Ibn al-Muthanna said: Abd al-A'la was in doubt.

And Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Sufyan ibn Uyaynah narrated to us, from Amr, from Ata', from Jabir, who said: We used to take provision of it all the way to Medina during the lifetime of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace).

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Zakariyya ibn Adi informed us, from Ubaydullah ibn Amr, from Zayd ibn Abi Unaysah, from Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from Jabir ibn Abdillah, who said: We used not to keep the meat of sacrificial animals beyond three days, but then the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) commanded us to take provisions from it and eat from it—meaning beyond three days.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Ali ibn Mushir narrated to us (H); and Yahya ibn Ayyub narrated to us: Ibn Ulayyah narrated to us, both from Ibn Jurayj, from Ata', from Jabir (H); and Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me—and the wording is his—: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj: Ata' narrated to us, who said: I heard Jabir ibn Abdillah saying: We used not to eat from the meat of our sacrificial camels beyond the three days of Mina, but then the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) gave us permission and said: "Eat and take provisions." I said to Ata': "Did Jabir say: 'until we arrived in Medina'?" He said: "Yes."

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us, he said: I read to Malik, from Abu az-Zubayr, from Jabir, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace): that he forbade eating the meat of sacrificial animals after three days, then he said later: "Eat, take provision, and store."

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali narrated to us: Rawh informed us: Malik narrated to us, from Abdallah ibn Abi Bakr, from Abdallah ibn Waqid, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade eating the meat of sacrificial animals after three days. Abdallah ibn Abi Bakr said: So I mentioned that to Amrah, and she said: "He spoke the truth; I heard A'ishah saying: Some bedouin families came in need during the time of al-Adha in the era of the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), so the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'Store for three days, then give in charity whatever remains.' Afterwards they said: 'O Messenger of Allah, people used to make water skins from their sacrificial animals and render melted fat from them.' The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: 'And what about that?' They said: 'You forbade that the meat of sacrificial animals be eaten after three days.' He said: 'I only forbade you because of the impoverished crowd that came; so eat, store, and give in charity.'"

And Ibn Abi Umar and Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us—Ibn Abi Umar said "narrated to us" and Abd said "informed us"—: Abd ar-Razzaq narrated to us: Ma'mar informed us, from az-Zuhri, from Salim, from Ibn Umar: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade that the meat of sacrificial animals be eaten after three days. Salim said: So Ibn Umar would not eat the meat of sacrificial animals beyond three days; and Ibn Abi Umar said: "after three days."

And Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Ibn Jurayj (H); and Muhammad ibn Rafi' narrated to me: Ibn Abi Fudayk narrated to us: ad-Dahhak—meaning Ibn Uthman—informed us, both from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), a narration similar to the hadith of al-Layth.

And Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us (H); and Muhammad ibn Rumh narrated to me: al-Layth informed us, from Nafi', from Ibn Umar, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), that he said: "None of you should eat from the meat of his sacrificial animal beyond three days."

And Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: the nephew of Ibn Shihab narrated to us (H); and Hasan al-Hulwani narrated to us: Ya'qub ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: my father narrated to us, from Salih (H); and Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: Abd ar-Razzaq informed us: Ma'mar informed us, all of them from az-Zuhri, with this chain of narration, a similar narration.

Harmalah ibn Yahya narrated to me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus narrated to me, from Ibn Shihab: Abu Ubayd, the freed slave of Ibn Azhar, narrated to me that he witnessed the Eid with Umar ibn al-Khattab. He said: Then I prayed with Ali ibn Abi Talib; he said: so he led us in prayer before the sermon, then addressed the people and said: "The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) has forbidden you from eating the meat of your sacrifices beyond three nights, so do not eat it."

Abd al-Jabbar ibn al-Ala' narrated to me: Sufyan narrated to us: az-Zuhri narrated to us, from Abu Ubayd, who said: I witnessed the Eid with Ali ibn Abi Talib; he started with the prayer before the sermon, and said: "The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) forbade us to eat from the meat of our sacrifices after three days."

And Muhammad ibn al-Walid ibn Abd al-Hamid narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us, from Sa'id ibn Masruq, from Abayah ibn Rifa'ah ibn Rafi', from Rafi' ibn Khadij, that he said: "O Messenger of Allah, we are encountering the enemy tomorrow and we have no knives with us..." and he related the hadith, but he did not mention: "so the people hurried and boiled the cooking pots with it, so he ordered them and they were overturned," and he mentioned the rest of the story.

And al-Qasim ibn Zakariyya narrated it to me: Husayn ibn Ali narrated to us, from Za'idah, from Sa'id ibn Masruq, with this chain of narration, the hadith to its end in full, and he said in it: "and we have no knives with us; may we slaughter with reeds?"

And Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us: Sufyan narrated to us, from Isma'il ibn Muslim, from Sa'id ibn Masruq, from Abayah, from his grandfather Rafi'. Then Umar ibn Sa'id ibn Masruq narrated it to me, from his father, from Abayah ibn Rifa'ah ibn Rafi' ibn Khadij, from his grandfather, who said: We said: "O Messenger of Allah, we are encountering the enemy tomorrow and we have no knives with us; may we slaughter with reed splinters?" And he mentioned the hadith with its story and said: "So a camel among them ran away from us, so we shot it with arrows until we incapacitated it."

And Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Waki' informed us: Sufyan ibn Sa'id ibn Masruq narrated to us, from his father, from Abayah ibn Rifa'ah ibn Rafi' ibn Khadij, from Rafi' ibn Khadij, who said: We were with the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) at Dhu al-Hulayfah in Tihamah, and we obtained some sheep and camels as booty. The people acted hastily and boiled cooking pots with them, so he ordered them and they were overturned, then he equated ten sheep to one camel... and he mentioned the rest of the hadith like the hadith of Yahya ibn Sa'id.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna al-Anazi narrated to us: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Sufyan: my father narrated to me, from Abayah ibn Rifa'ah ibn Rafi' ibn Khadij, from Rafi' ibn Khadij: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, we are encountering the enemy tomorrow and we have no knives with us." He (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Be quick, or let blood flow with whatever causes it to flow and mention the name of Allah upon it, and eat, provided it is not a tooth or a claw. And I will inform you: as for the tooth, it is a bone; and as for the claw, it is the knife of the Abyssinians." He said: And we captured booty of camels and sheep, and one camel from them ran wild, so a man shot it with an arrow and restrained it. Then the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Indeed, some of these camels run wild like wild beasts, so if any of them gets the better of you, do with it like this."

Harun ibn Ma'ruf narrated to us: Abdallah ibn Wahb narrated to us; he said: Haywah said: Abu Sakhr informed me, from Yazid ibn Qusayt, from Urwah ibn az-Zubayr, from A'ishah: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) commanded that a horned ram that stepped in black, knelt in black, and looked in black be brought for sacrifice. When it was brought to him to sacrifice it, he said to her: "O A'ishah, bring me the knife." Then he said: "Sharpen it with a stone." She did so, then he took it and took the ram, laid it down on its side, and slaughtered it. Then he said: "In the name of Allah. O Allah, accept from Muhammad, the family of Muhammad, and from the community of Muhammad." Then he offered it as sacrifice.

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Ibn Abi Adiyy narrated to us, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, from Anas, from the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), a similar narration, except that he said: and he would say: "In the name of Allah, and Allah is the Greatest."

And Yahya ibn Habib narrated to us: Khalid—meaning Ibn al-Harith—narrated to us: Shu'bah narrated to us: Qatadah informed me, who said: I heard Anas saying: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) offered sacrifice... a similar narration. He said: I asked: "Did you hear it from Anas?" He said: "Yes."

Yahya ibn Yahya narrated to us: Waki' informed us, from Shu'bah, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) sacrificed two horned rams with white and black markings. He said: And I saw him slaughtering them with his own hand, and I saw him placing his foot on their sides; he said: and he mentioned the name of Allah and declared His greatness.

Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Abu Awanah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Anas, who said: The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) sacrificed two horned rams with white and black markings; he slaughtered them with his own hand, mentioned the name of Allah, declared His greatness, and placed his foot on their sides.

And Abdallah ibn Abd ar-Rahman ad-Darimi narrated to me: Yahya—meaning Ibn Hassan—narrated to us: Mu'awiyah—and he is Ibn Sallam—informed us: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir narrated to me: Ba'jah ibn Abdillah informed me that Uqbah ibn Amir al-Juhani informed him that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) distributed sacrificial animals among his companions... with similar meaning.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, from Hisham ad-Dastawa'i, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Ba'jah al-Juhani, from Uqbah ibn Amir al-Juhani, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) distributed sacrificial animals among us, and a young animal fell to my lot. I said: "O Messenger of Allah, a young animal fell to my lot." So he said: "Sacrifice it."

And Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us (H); and Muhammad ibn Rumh narrated to us: al-Layth informed us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from Abu al-Khayr, from Uqbah ibn Amir: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) gave him sheep to distribute among his companions as sacrificial animals, and there remained a young billy goat. He mentioned it to the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace), so he said: "Sacrifice it yourself." Qutaybah said: "among his companions."

And Muhammad ibn Hatim narrated to me: Muhammad ibn Bakr narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj informed us: Abu az-Zubayr informed me that he heard Jabir ibn Abdillah saying: The Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) led us in prayer on the Day of Sacrifice in Medina. Some men stepped forward and slaughtered, thinking that the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) had already slaughtered. So the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) commanded whoever had slaughtered before him to repeat with another slaughter, and that they should not slaughter until the Prophet (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) had slaughtered.

Ahmad ibn Yunus narrated to us: Zuhayr narrated to us: Abu az-Zubayr narrated to us, from Jabir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) said: "Do not slaughter except a mature animal (musinnah), unless it becomes difficult for you, in which case you may slaughter a one-year-old sheep (jadha'ah)."

And Ziyad ibn Yahya al-Hassani narrated to me: Hatim—meaning Ibn Wardan—narrated to us: Ayyub narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Sirin, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: The Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) delivered a sermon to us on the Day of Adha; he said: and he smelled the scent of meat, so he forbade them to slaughter before the prayer and said: "Whoever has sacrificed, let him repeat." Then he mentioned a narration similar to their hadith.

Muhammad ibn Ubayd al-Ghubari narrated to us: Hammad ibn Zayd narrated to us: Ayyub and Hisham narrated to us, from Muhammad, from Anas ibn Malik: that the Messenger of Allah (may Allah bless him and grant him peace) prayed, then delivered a sermon and commanded whoever had slaughtered before the prayer to repeat the slaughter; then he mentioned a narration similar to the hadith of Ibn Ulayyah.
